summary.one_liner: A curated, link-only README listing programming tutorials in which readers build a complete application from scratch, grouped by language.
keywords: find a coding project to practice
sample apps to learn a language
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a Markdown list of programming tutorials where learners build an application from scratch. It has a table of contents with about 23 language sections (C#, C/C++, Go, JavaScript, Python, Rust, Swift and others) plus an Additional Resources section. Within each language, entries are grouped by domain or framework, for example Python is split into web scraping, web applications, bots, data science, machine learning, OpenCV and deep learning. Many entries are multi-part tutorials with sub-links for each part. The README links out to external tutorials and contains no code of its own. It also says that tutorials may involve multiple technologies and points readers to CONTRIBUTING.md for contribution guidelines.
use_cases: Find a project to build while learning a new language
Browse beginner-friendly app tutorials by language
Practice compilers, interpreters, or OS-level projects
Follow a multi-part tutorial such as a chat app or URL shortener
Find machine learning or OpenCV project walkthroughs
Pick a game or emulator project to build
how_to_run: Open README.md and browse the Table of Contents
Follow the external links to the tutorial you want
To contribute, fork the repo and read CONTRIBUTING.md
stack: Python (repository's main language per GitHub metadata)
notable: Covers about 23 languages with dozens of linked project tutorials
Multi-part tutorials are listed with sub-links for each part, such as a C compiler or a Linux debugger
Organized by language, with subsections by domain or framework (e.g. Python machine learning, Dart Flutter clones)
Includes a Network programming and OpenGL section under C/C++
caveats: Link-only list: it hosts no tutorial content itself, so linked pages may move, disappear, or go out of date (one entry is marked outdated and one as in progress)
Quality and depth vary by linked resource, and some links are videos or paid courses (Udemy is listed)
